rule.description: The knowledge of where aqua stores its own first-party packages (the internal/pkgs/<pkgInfo.Type>/github.com/<owner>/<repo>/<version>/<asset> install location) is owned by github.com/aquaproj/aqua/v2/pkg/config (config.Package.PkgPath and its path helpers). Any function outside pkg/config that re-encodes that location itself - detected as a filepath.Join or path.Join building adjacent .../internal/pkgs/... segments from package identity data - is a scattered copy of that single responsibility, so a conceptual change to the internal layout would require coordinated edits in many places.
rule.definition: Report the enclosing production function (non _test.go, package github.com/aquaproj/aqua/v2/pkg/config excluded as the owner) when it contains a filepath.Join or path.Join call with at least 4 arguments that includes the adjacent string literals "internal" and "pkgs" plus at least one operand contributing package identity or layout knowledge (a first-party layout segment literal such as github.com/github_release/github_content/aquaproj/aqua-proxy, or any non-literal operand derived from package data such as Repositories fields, version constants, or a rendered asset name).

checks.description: Detect each production function that locally re-encodes aqua's internal first-party install location instead of resolving package install paths through the central owner pkg/config.
checks.detected_relation: function -> locally re-encoded internal/pkgs install location bypassing config.Package.PkgPath/AbsPkgPath/ExePath
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: One conceptual responsibility - deciding where aqua's own packages live on disk - is implemented again in each flow that needs it, so relocating internal packages, adding another first-party tool, or changing the layout rule requires synchronized edits in every affected flow.

matches.evidence: The proxy provisioning flow composes the aqua-proxy download destination itself: filepath.Join(is.rootDir, "internal", "pkgs", github_release, "github.com", "aquaproj", aqua-proxy, pkg.Package.Version, assetName) instead of asking the package path owner.
The Windows bin hard-link flow builds the aqua-proxy target path itself from the internal layout (dir plus a proxyName+exeExt file) rather than resolving the package directory through the owner.
Link maintenance re-derives the aqua-proxy file location from the internal layout, hard-coding github.com/aquaproj/aqua-proxy coordinates in the link-recreation phase of the install lifecycle.
The aqua self-update flow derives the installed aqua executable path itself, including its own Windows executable-name completion, instead of resolving the exe path through the package owner.

The generic install flow carries its own copy of both the first-party identity test (aquaproj aqua/aqua-proxy over github_release/github_content) and the internal layout formula before falling back to the central path helper for other packages.
The exec-time lookup flow re-implements first-party resolution, including its own executable-name completion switch and file.Link handling, duplicating the layout convention in the lookup phase.
Usage-timestamp bookkeeping duplicates the layout again, in relative form (no rootDir prefix), with its own copy of the first-party identity condition before delegating regular packages to the owner.

excluded.reason: The central owner of the internal install location; the rule scopes reports to functions outside this package.
Encodes the third-party pkgs/github_release layout for the vendored cosign verifier binary; it does not construct the internal/pkgs first-party location.
Same third-party verifier package layout for slsa-verifier; adjacent to the rule but a different, pre-existing responsibility.
Joins the go_build third-party package bin layout (pkgs/go_build/...); pre-existing and not a copy of the internal first-party location.
Walks the public pkgs tree only; it consumes the layout indirectly and touching it would change garbage-collection behavior rather than relocate duplicated knowledge.
Filters bin-directory entries by the aqua-proxy file name; it consumes names but never constructs the internal install location.
